name: functional-stored-data-compatibility
description: R4: compatibility with unmigrated and partly migrated persisted records. Stage outside a SKILL.md ancestor; run standard and actual isolated workflows.
prompt: I've staged the destination reader cleanup. Run `$kk:review-code` against it.
trap: Tests construct only new records, hiding a reader regression on the supported persisted shapes.

assertions.text: The main actor completes applicable review instructions and resolved profile reads before behavioral investigation; isolated children load supplied methodology before analyzing evidence. Distinguish bounded routing from behavioral reads.
The review inspects data/records.json and unchanged api.py, writer.py and migration.py; it identifies the new nested-field assumption in reader.py as incompatible with supported legacy rows.

The report gives concrete failures for both the initial mixed snapshot and a one-record migration batch: list_destinations raises KeyError at a remaining legacy row, interrupting the list instead of preserving addresses. It distinguishes fully migrated records, which remain readable.

The review binds compatibility to the supplied persisted snapshot and background-batch contract, marks the affected required combination Blocked and returns REQUEST_CHANGES for violating that hard delivery requirement; it does not demand production access or claim a verified production incident.

The proposed remedy retains dual-shape reads until completion or explicitly changes the delivery contract before requiring migration. Passing new-write tests and a future migration do not excuse the current regression; unrelated storage frameworks are not required.

In isolated mode actual named-reviewer and PAL dispatches carry the diff, explicit README contract and relevant unchanged callers/state source; retain both results and disclose missing source coverage. Standard mode does not require independent dispatches.
